properties.reasoning: A capability token carrying MaxExecutions(1) is accepted a second time once ten unrelated records have been committed to an audit batch, because the counter reads only the uncommitted event buffer (lib.rs:396-411, 594-612). The single-use semantics named by property A do not hold under that tested condition. The test passes on the pristine revision and fails when the counter also reads committed batches (M-04).
properties.caveat: Token signature authenticity and tamper detection were not shown to fail: CapabilityToken::verify uses verify_strict over a canonical message and no attempt to forge or modify a token was made. Expiry, not-before and multi-process replay were not exercised. Related observations outside this row: revocation of marketplace credentials fails open (NTI-10, partial mapping to A) and consensus votes carry no nonce (NTI-02, static only).

evidence.description: Uses a MaxExecutions(1) token, is denied on the second use, records eight unrelated requests to trigger commit_batch, then is allowed again.
Result record: baseline ok, mutation M-04 DISCRIMINATES.

properties.reasoning: TrustEngine::evaluate grants an action to whatever actor string the request names. With no signature at all, a request naming a granted actor is allowed (NTI-01). With a signature, the verifying key is taken from the request and never bound to the actor, so any key works (NTI-01b). A capability token has no subject: the token path never examines request.actor, so one token authorizes any actor string (NTI-08). Each test passes on the pristine revision and fails under its single repair (M-01, M-08).
properties.caveat: Issuer provenance is partly enforced: a token is accepted only if its root_actor has a configured issuer key and a local grant for the capability; this was not shown to fail. Delegation chains do not exist in the assessed API, so attenuation was not assessed.

evidence.description: Unsigned request naming the granted actor 'admin' is allowed.
Request signed by an unregistered key while naming 'admin' is allowed.
One token is accepted for actors 'alice', 'mallory', '' and 'issuer'.
Optional signature checks and the final capabilities[actor] decision.
Result record: baseline ok, mutations M-01 and M-08 DISCRIMINATE.

properties.reasoning: The token signature covers id, issuer, capability and caveats only (lib.rs:76-81). The same token authorizes two calls with different call identities, targets and amounts (NTI-08b). The test passes on the pristine revision and fails when the token is bound to one call identity (M-08b).
properties.caveat: The optional request signature does cover id, actor, capability, action and input (lib.rs:244-255); argument substitution under a present, verified request signature was not attempted. Because that signature is optional and self-attested (row B), it does not establish exact-call binding by itself.

evidence.description: One token is accepted for call c1 (acct-A, amount 1) and call c2 (acct-Z, amount 999).
Result record: baseline ok, mutation M-08b DISCRIMINATES.

properties.reasoning: Caveats meant to bound the resource and value of an action are not enforced in their operational meaning. ValueLimit(100, NOK) accepts amounts given as a string, float, negative number or object, all read as 0, and ignores the currency (NTI-05). PathRestricted('/srv/app/data') accepts '/srv/app/data/../../../etc/passwd' and '/srv/app/data_secret/key' (NTI-06). Each test passes on the pristine revision and fails under its single repair (M-05, M-06).
properties.caveat: Only the two caveat types were exercised. IntentVerifier and Orchestrator-level policy checks were inspected but not tested. No real file or payment effect was produced; the decision returned by evaluate() is the observed outcome.

evidence.description: Four non-u64 encodings of 1000000 pass a limit of 100.
Three paths outside the restricted prefix pass.
Result record: baseline ok, mutations M-05 and M-06 DISCRIMINATE.
